zh.q: 桌上这一串东西，哪一段在「造」氨，哪一段在「收」氨？
zh.concl: 这就是教材第五章第二节「氨和铵盐」里的两套装置摆在一张台面上：一套造氨并收集（图5-13），一套拿这瓶氨做喷泉（图5-11）。
points: 从左到右就是操作顺序：造 → 干燥 → 收集 → 检验 → 喷泉。
① 段到 ② 段之间有导管连着，氨气是一路走过去的；③ 的烧瓶里装的是同样收集好的一瓶氨（虚线「同一瓶氨」：先收满、塞好塞子，再拿去做喷泉）。
教材图5-13 把「造」和「收」放在同一支试管里（管口塞棉花）；本课在教材图 5-13 的基础上加了一段干燥管，把它摊成「发生 → 干燥 → 收集」一条链——加干燥管是常见考法，教材图里没有。

zh.q: 加热固体的试管，口为什么不能朝上？
zh.concl: 加热固体时药品里的水蒸气会在管口冷凝；管口朝上时冷凝水会倒流到灼热的管底，可能使试管炸裂。教材图5-13 把管口画成略向下倾斜，正是为了让冷凝水流出去。
points: 「略向下倾斜」倾斜的是管口，不是管底——写成「管底略向下」是错的。
管口向上的问题不是「收不到氨」：氨照样产生，读数一点不变；危险在冷凝水会倒流到灼热的管底，试管可能炸裂。
棉花塞在管口，是防止固体粉末被气流带出去；它挡不住冷凝水。

zh.q: 中间这个干燥管里，能不能装浓硫酸？
zh.concl: 氨是碱性气体，遇到酸会生成铵盐（NH₃ + HCl = NH₄Cl）；浓硫酸是酸性干燥剂，会把氨全部吸掉，所以只能用碱石灰这类碱性干燥剂。
points: 干燥管要放在「发生」之后、「收集」之前——顺序错了等于没干燥。
判断干燥剂能不能用，看的是气体的酸碱性，不是「吸不吸水」。
教材 p.13–15 没有写干燥剂这一步，这一段是按「氨与酸反应生成铵盐」这条性质推出来的，界面不写成教材原话。

zh.q: 为什么这只集气瓶要瓶口朝下放？
zh.concl: 氨的密度比空气的小，瓶口朝下时氨沉在瓶里把空气顶出去；瓶口朝上则氨向上逸散，收不到。
points: 判断收集方法看密度：比空气小 → 瓶口向下收集；比空气大 → 瓶口向上收集。
「向下」说的是瓶口朝下，不是「把瓶子放低」。
9.3 % 不是「收得少一点」，是低于喷泉能形成的阈值——第 7 步会看到水几乎不动。

zh.q: 只收两分钟，够不够做喷泉？
zh.concl: 排空气法是「氨一点点把空气顶出去」，所以瓶内氨的体积分数随时间上升、先快后慢，收得越久越接近 95 % 的上限。
points: 体积分数上升是先快后慢（时间常数 2.5 min），不是匀速。
1 min 就过了 25 % 的形成阈值，但喷泉只升 3.8 cm（2 min 时 6.3 cm）——「能喷」与「喷得好」是两件事。
教材不给收集时间，这条曲线与这几个数是课件设定（示意），只用来讲趋势。

zh.q: 怎么知道这瓶收满了？瓶口那团白烟又是什么？
zh.concl: 氨遇氯化氢迅速反应生成氯化铵晶体（教材原话），所以看到的是白烟；氨水显弱碱性，能使红色石蕊试纸变蓝、酚酞变红——这就是验满与鉴定的依据。
points: 验满要用湿润的试纸：氨是气体，得先溶于水生成 NH₃·H₂O 并电离出 OH⁻ 才显碱性。
白烟是固体（NH₄Cl 小颗粒），不是白雾（液滴）——「烟」与「雾」不能混。
变蓝的是红色石蕊试纸（不是蓝色石蕊试纸）；酚酞要到第 7 步的喷泉才用。

zh.q: 只挤一下胶头滴管，水怎么就自己冲上去了？
zh.concl: 氨极易溶于水（1 体积水约溶 700 体积氨），水一进瓶，瓶内气体几乎全被吸进水里，瓶内压强骤降到远低于大气压，大气压就把烧杯里的水经玻璃管压进烧瓶，形成喷泉；氨水显弱碱性，酚酞变红。
points: 动力来自瓶内外的压强差，不是「水自己会往上流」。
喷泉是红色的：水里预先滴了酚酞，而氨水显弱碱性。
挤压胶头滴管那一点水只是引子——它让瓶里的氨有了能溶进去的水，之后的水是被大气压压进去的。

zh.q: 瓶子里到底少了什么，才让水被吸上去？
zh.concl: 氨分子极易溶于水并与水结合成一水合氨，一水合氨小部分电离出 NH₄⁺ 和 OH⁻；瓶里气体分子数骤减，压强随之骤降，大气压把水压进来。（教材【实验5-6】要求「分析出现这些现象的可能原因」，这段解释就是它的答案。）
points: 变的是气体分子数（分子跑进水里了），不是「瓶里的空气被抽走了」。
OH⁻ 是「氨水显碱性」的直接原因，酚酞变红就是它在起作用。
水进去的体积约等于氨原来占的体积，所以最后水面几乎顶到瓶颈。

zh.q: 考核：按教材把这瓶氨收到最干净，然后让它喷起来
zh.concl: 考核没有新结论：造得出、收得净，才喷得高——四件事（加热、管口、干燥剂、收集方式）加一个动作（挤压）缺一不可。
points: 收集方式最容易漏：一拨成瓶口向上，体积分数就掉到 9.3 %，低于 25 % 阈值，喷泉直接没了。
干燥剂与加热都会让体积分数归零，前几步做错这里就做不出来。
挤压只是引子：水能不能上来，取决于瓶里到底有多少氨。

en.q: Of this row of equipment on the bench, which part "makes" ammonia and which part "collects" it?
en.concl: These are the two setups from textbook Ch. 5, Sec. 2 "Ammonia and Ammonium Salts" on one bench: one to make and collect ammonia (Fig. 5-13), one to use that flask for a fountain (Fig. 5-11).
points: Left to right is the order of operations: make → dry → collect → test → fountain.

Sections ① and ② are joined by tubing, so the ammonia flows straight through; the flask at ③ holds a flask of ammonia collected the same way (the dashed "same flask of ammonia": fill it, stopper it, then use it for the fountain).

Textbook Fig. 5-13 makes and collects in one test tube (cotton plug at the mouth); this lesson adds a drying tube to Fig. 5-13, spreading it into a "generate → dry → collect" chain. Adding a drying tube is a common exam variant, not in the textbook figure.

en.q: Why can't the mouth of a test tube heating solids point upward?
en.concl: When heating solids, water vapor from the reagents condenses at the mouth; with the mouth up, the condensate flows back onto the hot bottom and may crack the tube. Textbook Fig. 5-13 draws the mouth tilted slightly down precisely so the condensate runs out.
points: "Tilted slightly down" refers to the mouth, not the bottom; writing "bottom slightly down" is wrong.
The problem with mouth up isn't "no ammonia": ammonia is still made and the reading doesn't change at all. The danger is that condensate flows back onto the hot bottom and the tube may crack.
The cotton at the mouth keeps solid powder from being carried out by the gas; it doesn't stop condensate.

en.q: Can the drying tube in the middle be filled with concentrated sulfuric acid?
en.concl: Ammonia is a basic gas that forms ammonium salts with acids (NH₃ + HCl = NH₄Cl); concentrated sulfuric acid is an acidic drying agent that would absorb all the ammonia, so only basic drying agents like soda lime will work.
points: The drying tube goes after "generate" and before "collect"; in the wrong order it doesn't dry anything.
Whether a drying agent works depends on the gas being acidic or basic, not on "does it absorb water".
Textbook pp.13–15 don't cover a drying step; this part is inferred from the property "ammonia reacts with acids to form ammonium salts", and the screen doesn't present it as textbook wording.

en.q: Why is this gas jar placed mouth down?
en.concl: Ammonia is less dense than air, so with the mouth down it fills the jar from the top and pushes the air out; with the mouth up it escapes upward and isn't collected.
points: Choose the collection method by density: lighter than air → collect mouth down; heavier than air → collect mouth up.
"Down" means the jar's mouth faces down, not "put the jar lower".
9.3 % isn't "a bit less"; it's below the fountain threshold, and in step 7 you'll see the water barely moves.

en.q: Is two minutes of collecting enough for a fountain?
en.concl: Air displacement means "ammonia gradually pushes the air out", so the ammonia fraction in the jar rises over time, fast at first and then slowly, approaching the 95 % ceiling the longer you collect.
points: The volume fraction rises fast at first, then slowly (time constant 2.5 min), not at a steady rate.
It passes the 25 % threshold within 1 min, but the fountain only rises 3.8 cm (6.3 cm at 2 min): "it sprays" and "it sprays well" are two different things.
The textbook gives no collection time; this curve and these numbers are lesson settings (illustrative), only to show the trend.

en.tag: Testing for full and white smoke
en.q: How do you know this jar is full? And what's the white smoke at the mouth?
en.concl: Ammonia reacts quickly with hydrogen chloride to form ammonium chloride crystals (textbook wording), so you see white smoke; ammonia water is weakly basic, turning red litmus blue and phenolphthalein red. This is the basis for checking and identifying it.
points: Use moist paper to check it's full: ammonia is a gas and only shows basicity after dissolving in water to form NH₃·H₂O, which ionizes to give OH⁻.
White smoke is a solid (NH₄Cl particles), not white mist (droplets); don't confuse "smoke" and "mist".
It's red litmus paper that turns blue (not blue litmus paper); phenolphthalein isn't used until the fountain in step 7.

en.q: You only squeeze the dropper once. How does the water rush up by itself?
en.concl: Ammonia is extremely soluble in water (1 volume of water dissolves about 700 volumes of ammonia). Once water enters the flask, almost all the gas dissolves, the flask pressure plunges far below atmospheric, and air pressure pushes water from the beaker up the glass tube into the flask, making a fountain; ammonia water is weakly basic, so phenolphthalein turns red.
points: The force comes from the pressure difference between inside and outside the flask, not "water flowing upward by itself".
The fountain is red: phenolphthalein was added to the water beforehand, and ammonia water is weakly basic.
The little water from the dropper is just a starter: it gives the ammonia some water to dissolve in; the rest of the water is pushed in by air pressure.

en.q: What exactly went missing from the flask to make the water rise?
en.concl: Ammonia molecules are extremely soluble and combine with water to form ammonia monohydrate, a small part of which ionizes to NH₄⁺ and OH⁻; the number of gas molecules in the flask plunges, the pressure plunges with it, and air pressure pushes the water in. (Textbook Exp. 5-6 asks you to "analyze the possible causes of these phenomena"; this explanation is the answer.)
points: What changes is the number of gas molecules (they went into the water), not "the air in the flask was pumped out".
OH⁻ is the direct reason "ammonia water is basic", and it's what turns phenolphthalein red.
The volume of water entering is about the volume the ammonia took up, so in the end the water nearly reaches the neck.

en.q: Assessment: collect this flask of ammonia as cleanly as the textbook does, then make it spray
en.concl: The assessment has no new conclusion: make it, collect it clean, and only then does it spray high. Four conditions (heating, mouth, drying agent, collection method) plus one action (squeezing), and none can be missing.
points: The collection method is the easiest to miss: switch to mouth up and the fraction drops to 9.3 %, below the 25 % threshold, and the fountain is gone.
The drying agent and heating can both send the fraction to zero; if earlier steps are wrong, this one won't work.
Squeezing is only the starter: whether the water rises depends on how much ammonia is actually in the flask.
